turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey Marcus, you got a sec? I need to run something by you.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sure, what's up? You look like you've been staring at a screen for twelve hours.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Close. I just finished the schema migration for the customer service DB. It's live now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, you did that already? I thought we were reviewing the rollback plan on Thursday.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I know, but the maintenance window opened at 2 AM and I figured I'd just get it done. It went smoothly — no locks, nothing blocked. The whole thing finished without locking a single table.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's... good? But did you take a backup first? Because the last time we did a schema change without one, we had to rebuild three days of transactions.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Honestly? I didn't. I thought the snapshot from last week was enough. But I checked the data after, and it looks fine.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Priya, 'looks fine' is not a backup. If something's corrupted, we're dead in the water. Let me pull a quick sanity check on a few customer records.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, I ran a sample query on the customer table. We have a problem.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: What kind of problem?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: About 200 records have null addresses and mismatched account IDs. The migration corrupted them. I'm looking at the logs now — it looks like the foreign key constraints got dropped mid-write.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Oh no. That's... that's bad. I really thought the no-lock thing meant it was safe.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: No-lock just means it didn't block other queries. It doesn't mean it was correct. We need to restore from that old snapshot, but you said you didn't take a fresh backup.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I know. I'm an idiot. Can we at least fix the corrupted rows manually? I have the original CSV exports from last month.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a band-aid. But let's do it — and then we need to tell the team. Also, for the love of god, never run a migration without a backup again.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey, so I fixed the corrupted records last night. But I have to confess something else.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What now?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: When I deployed the fix to production, I did it during peak hours — around 10 AM. I thought it was a small patch, so it wouldn't matter.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: You did what? Peak hours? Priya, that's when we have the most traffic. Did you even check the load balancer?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I didn't. And... the release caused an outage. For about twenty minutes, the entire customer portal was down. I got three alerts and then my phone wouldn't stop buzzing.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So let me get this straight: you migrated without a backup, corrupted records, ran it in a maintenance window but didn't lock anything, and then deployed during peak hours and took down the site. Is that about right?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yes. That's exactly right. I'm sorry. I think I need to step back and write a proper runbook before I touch anything else.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yeah, you do. And I'm going to be the one reviewing it. Let's start with a checklist: backup, lock, test, deploy off-peak. In that order.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Deal. And thank you for not yelling at me more than I already am yelling at myself.
